title: POC: Benchmark workload matrix & streaming vs non-streaming decision
summary: AE + SE run through POC success criteria and a workload matrix to size benchmark runs. Main decisions: incorporate two customer script sets (interactive chat + batch summarization), run cross-model comparators, and evaluate streaming for low-latency interactive flows. Timeline target: 3-week benchmark phase then 4-week pilot. Action items assigned for scripts, test harness access, and security docs.
next_steps: Redwood to provision benchmark sandbox + harness access (credentials emailed)
Customer to drop two canonical script packs into shared drive and add sample payloads
Schedule 1-hour deep-dive on streaming telemetry with SE next Wed
action_items: Maya Chen: send sandbox credentials and benchmark template (due: 2025-10-24)
Emily Wong: upload chat-script pack + batch summarization scripts to shared drive (due: 2025-10-24)
Diego Alvarez: prepare streaming telemetry deep-dive deck and example trace collection (due: 2025-10-27)
Samir Rao: confirm IP allowlist and KMS config for private benchmarking (due: 2025-10-28)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-22
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Hannah (Redwood CSM), Raj (CTO, Aurelia), Emily (ML Eng), Samir (SRE), Lena (PM), plus one generic speaker line

00:00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. quick round-robin — Maya from Redwood, Diego our SE, Hannah on CS. Raj, want to kick off?
00:00:14 Raj: Sure, thanks. So context: Aurelia's building a multi-tenant summarization and chat assistant for financial analysts. We have two distinct traffic profiles — interactive chat (low tokens/session, high concurrency, strong p95 SLA) and nightly batch summarization (large tokens, throughput-oriented). We're evaluating Redwood for a POC to validate latency/cost tradeoffs and to get a recommended serving configuration.
00:00:42 Diego: Great, that maps to the workload matrix we sent earlier. For the POC we typically run separate benchmark buckets: interactive (streaming enabled), and batch (non-streaming, large request payloads). But we also compare streaming vs non-streaming for interactive since sometimes customers prefer simpler non-streamed logic.
00:01:02 Emily: Quick question — our current models are a mix of open weights fine-tuned in-house and a provider model for fallback. We'll want to include both in the benchmarks. Can Redwood hit both hosted and dedicated variants?
00:01:18 Maya: Yes. For the POC we'll do hosted endpoints for speed, and we can also spin up a dedicated pool if you want to test sustained throughput under commit. For the benchmark phase we usually start hosted to iterate fast. If you need private networking we can provide a VPC sandbox.
00:01:36 Samir: We will need the VPC option — even for benchmarking, any traffic with customer PII has to remain within our network. Also KMS integration.
00:01:46 Hannah: Noted — we'll include KMS integration as part of the tasks. Diego, can you detail the harness integration expectations?
00:01:57 Diego: Sure. For harness we support: 1) our reference harness (Python CLI + YAML workload spec), 2) a JMeter/locust adapter if you prefer JVM-based tooling, 3) direct script run where you drop the customer scripts and we run them inside a container. The harness accepts two kinds of workloads: scenario scripts (step-by-step chat transcripts) and batch payload files (JSONL). The key is that scripts need to include timing metadata for realistic think times.
00:02:30 Lena: On think times — our chat clients have a ~700ms user think time median; peak bursts of around 250 concurrent users. Latency SLO is p95 < 450ms for the web UI.
00:02:42 Diego: Important note — p95 numbers are measured server-side excluding network egress; for streaming endpoints p95 refers to first-token latency or end-to-end? We should clarify.
00:02:55 Raj: We care about time-to-first-token for chat as that's what our UI shows. For batch, we care about end-to-end throughput per hour.
00:03:07 Diego: OK, so we'll include both metrics. For streaming we capture time-to-first-token (TTFT) and sustained token-per-second. For non-streamed we capture total response time and peak throughput.
00:03:22 Maya: Can we agree on baseline success criteria for the POC? What would make this a success for Aurelia?
00:03:29 Raj: Three things: (1) interactive p95 TTFT < 500ms at 250 conc with our typical prompt sizes, (2) batch pipeline can process 1.2M tokens/hour per node or show a path to that with dedicated capacity, and (3) clear cost estimates and operation runbook for switching to dedicated if needed.
00:03:48 Emily: Also regression checks — we need a quality baseline. We'll use our eval prompts against your generated outputs and compare quality metrics (ROUGE/semantic sim). We want to ensure quantization or batching doesn't degrade output beyond x% on our metrics.
00:04:05 Diego: We'll wire QA evaluations into the harness run — the harness can call your eval runner and attach quality metrics to each model/config run. We record the token-level cost too.
00:04:16 Samir: Security checklist — SOC2, audit logs, SSO/SAML for account access, and an IP allowlist for the sandbox.
00:04:25 Maya: We'll share SOC2 artifacts and an abbreviated security packet after the call.
00:04:30 Speaker 6: (inaudible)
00:04:42 Diego: For workload sizing I'd like to propose a "workload matrix" approach: rows are workload profiles (chat-light, chat-heavy, batch-large), columns are model/config variants (open-quantized, open-fp16, hosted-commercial), and cells define concurrency and token sizes. We'll run a prioritized sweep: first baseline chat at 50/150/250 conc, then streaming vs non-streaming at 250 conc, finally batch sizing across 4 payload sizes.
00:05:12 Lena: Sounds good. Timeline?
00:05:16 Maya: We can provision the sandbox tomorrow if approvals are quick. Realistically the benchmark run takes about 7-10 days to get repeatable numbers if we do full cross-product. Your target timeline is?
00:05:27 Raj: We were hoping to finish the benchmark phase in three weeks, then a 4-week pilot under dedicated capacity if numbers look good. So 7 weeks total.
00:05:34 Maya: That's feasible. We'll aim to start harness runs by Monday (2025-10-27) if Emily uploads scripts this week.
00:05:42 Emily: I'll upload two script packs today: chat-canonical (500 sessions) and batch-summaries (10k items). Expect a few sensitive record placeholders — I'll mark redaction instructions.
00:05:52 Diego: Great. On the streaming vs non-streaming decision — pros/cons quick: streaming reduces TTFT and perceived latency but complicates client-side logic and telemetry. Non-streaming is simpler, sometimes better cost per-run for small outputs. We'll quantify cost delta in the POC.
00:06:12 Raj: Any gotchas for KV cache with long-running chat? We want to leverage KV caching to reduce repeated prompts cost.
00:06:20 Diego: KV cache is supported for our runtime; it's primarily effective if sessions reuse prefix tokens. We'll include a variant with warm KV caches and cold starts. Also we'll test different cache sizes to see hit-rate impacts.
00:06:34 Lena: For the harness, will the scripts be modified or will Redwood run them as-is? We need to maintain our instrumentation.
00:06:41 Maya: We prefer you upload scripts as-is; our team will run them in an instrumented container that streams logs and metrics back to Redwood Console. We do not modify business logic. If optional wrappers are needed for telemetry, we'll work that through.
00:06:57 Emily: We insist on a read-only execution environment and that logs containing PII are redacted before leaving the container.
00:07:06 Hannah: We'll provide a runbook that explains log redaction options; the sandbox can be configured to redact at source.
00:07:12 Diego: On the metrics side we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-tokens, error rates (5xx), and quality evaluation scores. We'll also emit traces for streaming sessions to measure time-to-first-byte and first-token.
00:07:30 Raj: Good. For benchmarks, do you support running multiple models concurrently in the same pool for routing? We want to simulate fallback behavior where we route to a cheaper model on overload.
00:07:42 Diego: Yes — routing policies can be included. We can simulate fallback to a smaller model during simulated overload and measure user impact. We'll add a routing-policy cell in the workload matrix.
00:07:53 Maya: Let's talk about success thresholds we commit to reporting: we will report measured metrics plus a narrative of tradeoffs and recommended production config.
00:08:02 Lena: Also include runbook steps to flip to dedicated and implications for cost and latency.
00:08:07 Maya: Yep. Any blockers?
00:08:10 Samir: Only the IP allowlist and KMS details — we need to confirm network egress rules for the sandbox.
00:08:17 Maya: We'll include network details in the credentials email.
00:08:21 Diego: Operational detail — harness will run 3 identical runs per cell to compute variance. That will give us confidence intervals for p95.
00:08:30 Emily: How do you surface tokenization differences across models? Our prompts tokenize differently on our in-house models.
00:08:39 Diego: Harness will include a tokenizer step so we report token counts per-model and normalize cost by actual tokenization per model.
00:08:46 Raj: OK good. Anything about billing?
00:08:49 Maya: For POC benchmarks we provide a credits allocation; if you want sustained dedicated capacity during pilot we'll convert to a reserved contract. We'll provide ballpark cost estimates after runs.
00:09:00 Lena: One more question — are streaming endpoints priced differently?
00:09:04 Maya: Pricing depends on tokens and instance types; we report cost-per-token and also any streaming-specific overhead in the results.
00:09:12 Diego: Technical caveat — some quantized kernels have slightly different perf characteristics for streaming vs non-streaming; we'll note that in the results.
00:09:21 Speaker 6: (laughs)
00:09:27 Maya: Alright let's recap and assign actions. Recap: Redwood will provision sandbox + harness; customer uploads scripts; Redwood runs workload matrix including streaming vs non-streaming comparisons; deliverables are benchmark report + quality evals + runbook; timeline ~3 weeks for benchmarks.
00:09:47 Raj: That works. We'll aim to upload scripts by COB.
00:09:51 Maya: Diego will schedule the streaming telemetry deep dive next Wed.
00:09:55 Diego: I'll send calendar invite.
00:09:58 Hannah: I'll attach SOC2 + security packet to the follow-up email.
00:10:03 Maya: Anything else?
00:10:06 Emily: One ask: include an example of the harness YAML so we can prefill our config.
00:10:11 Diego: I'll attach a sample YAML in the follow-up.
00:10:15 Maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with credentials and next steps.
00:10:21 Raj: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
